userStories.title: Fix raw JSON displayed in chat widget when LLM returns JSON format
userStories.description: chatWithToolsLoop returns the raw LLM content string without checking if it is JSON. When the LLM responds in the old structured format {'intent':'menu_query','action':'llm_reply','response':'...','confidence':0.0}, the entire JSON string is sent to the chat widget and rendered verbatim (Image 4 bug). Fix: add a looksLikeJson guard in chatWithToolsLoop — if content looks like JSON, try to extract the 'response' or 'text' field; if none found, use the profile fallback.

technicalNotes: Edit src/assistant/ai-response-generator.ts: in chatWithToolsLoop, at line 141 where `return content || UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en`, add guard: if (content && looksLikeJson(content)) { try { const j = JSON.parse(content); const extracted = j.response || j.text || j.message || null; if (extracted && typeof extracted === 'string' && !looksLikeJson(extracted)) return extracted; } catch {} return UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en; } return content || UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_MESSAGES.en

userStories.title: Profile-scoped admin tab URLs: every tab includes profileId in hash
userStories.description: The admin panel URL only encodes the tab name (e.g. #intents, #responses) but never the active profile. Switching from hostel to cafe profile only updates localStorage — the URL stays the same. Fix: update all profile-specific tabs to include profileId in the URL (#intents/makan-moments, #responses/pelangi, etc.) following the pattern already used by #dashboard/makan-moments/tests. Switching profiles updates the URL; loading a URL auto-switches to the correct profile. Global tabs (settings, whatsapp, staff-review, help) keep the current flat URL.

userStories.title: Template variable interpolation in static reply messages ({{guestName}}, etc.)
userStories.description: Static replies send fixed text strings with no personalization. Support for template variables like {{guestName}}, {{checkInDate}}, and {{profileName}} would allow staff to create personalized automated responses without LLM calls, improving quality while keeping latency near zero for common greetings and confirmations.
acceptanceCriteria: Static reply templates can include {{variableName}} placeholders in their text content
On send, available variables (guestName, checkInDate, checkOutDate, profileName) are resolved from session context
Unresolvable variables fall back to an empty string or configurable default (e.g., 'our valued guest')
Admin editor shows a popover listing supported {{variables}} when editing a static reply text field
Variable substitution is applied before the message is sent; the raw template is stored in the config
Existing static replies without variables continue to work unchanged
technicalNotes: Implement an interpolate(template: string, variables: Record<string, string>) utility in src/assistant/
Variable context: profileName from settings.json; guest data from active session if tool result is available
Apply interpolation in the static_reply action handler just before message delivery
Admin UI change: add a help tooltip showing {{guestName}}, {{checkInDate}}, {{profileName}} as supported vars

userStories.title: Server-Sent Events streaming for progressive AI responses in webchat widget
userStories.description: The webchat widget waits for the full AI response before displaying it, causing a blank 3-10 second wait. Industry best practice is to stream AI tokens progressively using SSE or chunked transfer, reducing perceived latency to near-instant first-token display. Both OpenRouter and NVIDIA providers support OpenAI-compatible streaming.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/chat/:profileId/message returns a streaming SSE response for LLM-generated replies
The webchat.html renders tokens as they arrive, appending to the current assistant message bubble
A typing indicator (animated dots) is shown from message submission until the first token arrives
Streaming falls back gracefully to non-streaming single response if the provider does not support it
Static replies (pre-written responses) return instantly with no streaming overhead
Streaming works correctly with tool calls: tools execute server-side, then response text streams after
technicalNotes: Use EventSource (SSE) on client with text/event-stream content type on server
OpenRouter streaming: add stream: true to completions request, pipe response chunks as SSE events
NVIDIA NIM/Kimi K2.5 supports OpenAI-compatible streaming via the same stream: true flag
Tool calls must complete before streaming text phase begins (tool results are not streamed to client)
Add X-Accel-Buffering: no header for Nginx proxy compatibility with SSE

userStories.title: Complete webhook event routing to registered notification handlers
userStories.description: The webhook routing code in src/routes/webhooks/index.ts has TODO comments indicating that event-type routing and handler dispatch are not implemented. Inbound webhook events from external systems are received by the server but silently dropped with no handler execution, making the webhook integration feature non-functional.
acceptanceCriteria: Inbound webhook POST requests are dispatched to the correct handler function based on the event type field
A handler registry maps event type strings to async handler functions (at minimum one working handler)
Unrecognized event types return HTTP 422 with a descriptive error message and are logged
Handler errors are caught, logged, and return HTTP 500 without crashing the Express server
HMAC signature verification is enforced for all inbound webhook requests (or clearly documented as not required)
Vitest unit tests cover: correct handler dispatch, unrecognized event 422 response, and handler error 500 response
technicalNotes: Remove TODO comments in src/routes/webhooks/index.ts and implement a handler dispatch map
Follow existing route patterns in src/routes/admin/ for consistent error handling and response shapes
Add WEBHOOK_SECRET env var for HMAC-SHA256 signature verification if not already present
Implement at minimum a payment_confirmed handler that sends a WhatsApp confirmation message

userStories.title: Sentiment-based early escalation trigger in message processing pipeline
userStories.description: Current escalation triggers are intent-based, requiring users to explicitly request help. Frustrated or angry language is not detected, meaning the bot continues attempting to handle the situation without proactive human handoff. A lightweight sentiment check before intent classification enables early escalation before frustration peaks.
acceptanceCriteria: Messages containing strong negative sentiment markers are detected in the pipeline before intent classification
If a user sends 3 or more messages with negative sentiment in a single session, the pipeline escalates to human
The escalation message to the user is empathetic and acknowledges frustration (configurable per profile)
Sentiment detection can be enabled or disabled per profile in admin settings
Sentiment-triggered escalation events are recorded in escalation_events table with reason='sentiment'
Sentiment detection does not add more than 50ms to the average message processing time
technicalNotes: Use a rule-based keyword/phrase list (not a separate LLM call) to avoid latency and cost
Initial negative marker set (EN): 'useless', 'terrible', 'awful', 'angry', 'never again', repeated '!!', 'ridiculous'
Track consecutive_negative_messages counter in session context (in-memory, not persisted to DB)
Add sentiment_escalation_enabled and sentiment_threshold to profile settings.json
Optional: include sentiment as a classified field in existing intent classification LLM prompt to avoid extra round-trip

userStories.title: Restore prior conversation history on webchat widget page reload
userStories.description: When a user reloads the page or navigates away and returns to the webchat, the conversation history disappears even though a sessionId is stored in localStorage. Re-fetching and rendering prior messages on load reduces user frustration from having to repeat their queries and provides a professional chat experience.
acceptanceCriteria: On widget initialization, if a sessionId exists in localStorage, the last 10 messages are fetched from the server
Fetched messages are rendered in the chat UI in chronological order before the input is enabled
A subtle visual divider labeled 'Previous conversation' separates restored history from the current session
History fetch fails gracefully: if the endpoint errors, the widget opens empty without displaying an error
History restoration is limited to 10 messages to avoid overwhelming the UI
Session continuity works across page refreshes within the same browser but not across different devices
technicalNotes: Add GET /api/chat/:profileId/history?sessionId=xxx endpoint returning last 10 messages
Defer the history fetch to widget open event (not initial page load) to avoid unnecessary requests
Webchat sessions already use sessionId in localStorage; use this as the message lookup key
rainbow_messages stores by phone field; for webchat, sessionId is used as the 'phone' equivalent

userStories.title: Intent coverage gap analysis: surface high-frequency unmatched patterns in admin
userStories.description: When AI cannot match an intent, the unmatched message content is not surfaced for review. Clustering unmatched messages by topic reveals systematic coverage gaps, allowing staff to add intents or KB articles for the most common unanswered questions, directly improving resolution rate.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin analytics panel has an Intent Gaps section showing the top 10 message patterns that triggered unknownFallback
Patterns are grouped by approximate semantic similarity or keyword frequency
Each gap cluster shows: an example message, count in last 30 days, and a Create Intent shortcut button
The Create Intent shortcut pre-fills the new intent dialog with the example message as a sample utterance
Gap analysis is scoped per profile (not aggregated globally)
Data is derived from message content stored when unknownFallback is triggered
technicalNotes: Store raw message text in intent_analytics when intent matches unknownFallback (add message_content column if missing)
MVP clustering: count word frequency across unmatched messages, return top 10 most common terms with examples
Add GET /api/admin/analytics/intent-gaps?profileId=&days=30 endpoint
Use existing intent editor component to handle the Create Intent shortcut with pre-filled utterance

userStories.title: Automated daily chatbot performance summary sent to admin via WhatsApp
userStories.description: Operators have no passive visibility into daily Rainbow AI performance without actively opening the admin panel. An automated daily WhatsApp summary to the admin number provides a zero-effort overview of conversation volume, resolution rate, top intents, and any active alerts.
acceptanceCriteria: A daily report is sent to a configured admin WhatsApp number at a configurable time (default 8AM local)
Report includes: total conversations in last 24h, AI resolution rate %, human handoffs count, top 3 intents, and fallback rate
Report is per-profile or cross-profile summary based on configuration
Report is only sent if at least 1 conversation occurred in the last 24 hours
Admin can enable/disable daily reports and set the delivery time in admin settings panel
Report delivery timestamp and status are logged for review
technicalNotes: Add a report generation function querying intent_analytics, escalation_events, rainbow_conversations
Schedule using existing cron/scheduler infrastructure
Send via Baileys existing sendMessage function (already used for escalation notifications)
Format as plain WhatsApp text using *bold* markdown, no HTML
Add daily_report block to settings.json: enabled, recipient_phone, send_time (HH:MM)

userStories.title: Webchat session idle timeout with configurable re-engagement message
userStories.description: Webchat sessions that go idle do not close gracefully or send re-engagement messages, leaving sessions open indefinitely and inflating active session counts. Best practice is a configurable idle timeout that sends a gentle re-engagement message before marking the session as timed out.
acceptanceCriteria: Webchat sessions idle for more than the configured timeout (default 30 minutes) receive a re-engagement message
Re-engagement message text is configurable per profile in admin settings
If the user does not respond within 10 minutes of the re-engagement message, the session is marked as timed_out
Timed-out sessions are tracked in the database and excluded from active session count metrics
Session timeout duration is configurable per profile (default 30 minutes, min 5 minutes)
Re-engagement and timeout apply to webchat sessions only, NOT WhatsApp (where Meta manages session windows)
technicalNotes: Track last_activity_at on webchat sessions (add column to rainbow_conversations or a webchat_sessions table)
Implement a lazy-check approach: check idle time on each incoming message rather than a polling loop
Send re-engagement via existing webchat message delivery mechanism
Add session_timeout_minutes and reengagement_message fields to webchat profile settings.json block

userStories.title: Profile configuration cloning: duplicate an existing profile as a starting template
userStories.description: Creating a new business profile requires manually recreating all routing rules, intents, static replies, KB files, and settings. A profile clone feature lets operators create a new profile from an existing one as a template, dramatically reducing setup time when adding new properties or brands.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin profile management view has a Clone Profile action for each existing profile
Cloning copies routing.json, knowledge.json, settings.json, and intent configs from the source profile
Cloned profile receives a new unique profileId and a user-specified display name
WhatsApp auth state is NOT copied (cloned profile starts without a connected phone number)
Admin sees a confirmation dialog listing exactly what will be copied before proceeding
Clone operation completes within 5 seconds and navigates admin to the new profile
technicalNotes: Add POST /api/admin/profiles/:sourceId/clone endpoint with { newProfileId, displayName } body
Deep-copy the source profile's rainbow_configs rows inserting with the new profileId prefix
Copy rainbow_kb_files metadata rows with the new profileId; do not copy actual KB file content on disk
Exclude whatsapp-auth/ directory and phone-number-specific settings from the clone
Return the new profileId so the admin panel can navigate directly to the cloned profile settings

userStories.title: Admin UI for per-profile WhatsApp frequency cap and rate limit configuration
userStories.description: Frequency cap rules (limiting outbound messages per user per day) exist as API-only settings with no admin UI. Staff cannot view or modify these rules without developer access, making the feature invisible to operators and preventing appropriate rate-limit tuning for different property types.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin Settings panel has a Rate Limits section showing current frequency cap rules per profile
Admin can set the maximum outbound messages per user per 24-hour window via a numeric input
Admin can enable or disable rate limiting per profile without any code changes
When a rate limit is hit, the admin shows a count of rate-limited users in the last 24 hours
Settings changes take effect within 1 minute without requiring a server restart
Settings are persisted to rainbow_configs (the existing config persistence layer)
technicalNotes: Add a rate_limits section to settings.json schema with max_messages_per_user_per_24h and enabled fields
Add admin UI component in Settings tab: numeric input for max_messages_per_user_per_day + toggle
Rate limit enforcement logic already exists in the codebase; UI connects to the same settings.json config
Add GET /api/admin/rate-limits/stats?profileId= returning count of users who hit the cap in last 24h

userStories.title: Emit WhatsApp typing indicator during AI processing delay
userStories.description: When Rainbow AI receives a WhatsApp message and begins processing, send a typing indicator (chat presence 'composing') to the sender immediately, then clear it when the reply is sent. Without this, users see dead silence for 2-6 seconds between sending and receiving a reply, causing perceived unresponsiveness and drop-offs.
acceptanceCriteria: On every incoming WhatsApp message, `sendWhatsAppTypingIndicator` is called with `composing` state before pipeline processing begins
Typing indicator is cleared (paused state sent) immediately when the bot reply is dispatched
If processing takes over 20 seconds the indicator is re-sent to prevent WhatsApp's 25-second auto-dismiss
Typing indicator is NOT sent if the message is silently dropped (duplicate, system message, or ignored group message)
Behaviour is configurable per-profile via settings.json `features.typingIndicator: true|false`
technicalNotes: `sendWhatsAppTypingIndicator` already exists in `src/lib/whatsapp/index.ts` — integrate into `src/assistant/message-router.ts` before pipeline dispatch
Baileys API: `sock.sendPresenceUpdate('composing', jid)` and `sock.sendPresenceUpdate('paused', jid)`
Gate behind `delay > 500ms` check to avoid unnecessary presence updates for instant cached replies

userStories.title: Baileys circuit breaker: long cooldown after consecutive reconnect failures
userStories.description: The current reconnect logic (3 attempts, max 60s delay) is insufficient to prevent WhatsApp account bans caused by rapid connect/disconnect cycling. When the supervisor and Baileys instance both retry simultaneously, hundreds of failed handshakes can trigger abuse detection. A circuit breaker must open after N consecutive failures and enforce a 30-minute cooldown.
acceptanceCriteria: After 5 consecutive connection failures (configurable), the circuit opens and no further reconnection is attempted for 30 minutes
A WARNING-level log is emitted: `[Baileys:id] Circuit breaker OPEN — 5 consecutive failures. Cooling down for 30 min.`
An admin WhatsApp notification is sent when the circuit opens
After the 30-minute cooldown the circuit enters HALF-OPEN, attempts one reconnection, and either closes (success) or reopens with another 30-min cooldown
Circuit state (open/closed/half-open, last-open timestamp, failure count) is exposed on `GET /api/rainbow/status` per instance
technicalNotes: Implement inside `src/lib/whatsapp/instance.ts` `handleDisconnect()` — replace current 3-attempt counter with a circuit-breaker state machine
Separate from `baileys-supervisor.ts` which handles supervisor-level crashes — this is instance-level connection cycling
Use `Date.now()` timestamps rather than a library; no external dependency needed

userStories.title: Monitor WhatsApp message template quality and alert on pause/disable
userStories.description: When Meta automatically pauses a template due to low quality rating (spam reports, low read rate), the bot silently fails to deliver proactive messages. A webhook listener and admin alert must detect template pauses before they escalate to permanent disable.
acceptanceCriteria: Incoming `message_template_status_update` webhook events are parsed and persisted to a `template_quality_events` DB table with fields: template_name, old_status, new_status, reason, timestamp
When a template status changes to PAUSED or DISABLED, an admin WhatsApp notification is sent within 60 seconds including template name, new status, and pause duration
Admin dashboard shows current status and quality rating for each registered template
A daily summary of template quality ratings is included in the existing daily performance report
Webhook handler returns HTTP 200 within 5 seconds to avoid Meta retry storms
technicalNotes: Meta sends `message_template_status_update` to the registered webhook — add handler to `src/routes/webhooks/index.ts`
This is a Meta Cloud API webhook, not a Baileys event — requires Meta webhook subscription to include `message_template_status_update` field
Distinct from existing phone number quality tracking in `src/lib/phone-quality.ts`

userStories.title: PDPA/GDPR data portability endpoint: export all personal data by JID
userStories.description: Malaysia's amended PDPA (effective June 2025) grants data subjects the right to request their personal data in a portable, machine-readable format. The existing GDPR erasure endpoint handles deletion, but there is no corresponding data export endpoint. Businesses processing data from over 20,000 contacts are now legally obligated to fulfil portability requests.
acceptanceCriteria: New endpoint `GET /api/rainbow/guests/:jid/data-export` returns all personal data for the JID as structured JSON
Export includes: all messages (content, timestamps, direction), conversation metadata, intent predictions, feedback records, opt-out status, and conversation state
Response includes a `generated_at` ISO timestamp and `retention_policy` summary
Request is logged to `gdpr_audit_log` table with `action: 'data_export'`
Endpoint requires admin authentication (same auth as erasure endpoint)
Response time under 5 seconds for up to 10,000 messages; returns 202 with a job ID for larger datasets
technicalNotes: Mirror the query pattern from `src/routes/admin/gdpr-erasure.ts` but SELECT instead of DELETE
Canonicalize the JID using `canonicalPhoneKey()` before querying — same as erasure endpoint
Use `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=data-export-{hash}.json` header for download

userStories.title: Per-JID inbound message rate limiter to prevent bot abuse
userStories.description: A single WhatsApp number can flood the bot with hundreds of messages per minute, exhausting AI provider quotas and degrading service for all users. The existing rate limiter operates at a profile level, not per individual user JID. A sliding-window per-JID limiter should throttle abusive senders with a polite rejection message.
acceptanceCriteria: Each unique sender JID is limited to 10 messages per 60-second sliding window (configurable per profile in settings.json)
When the limit is exceeded, the bot sends one brief reply: 'Too many messages — please wait a moment before sending more.' and drops subsequent messages until the window resets
The throttle reply is sent at most once per window (not once per dropped message)
Rate limit counters are in-memory (not Redis-dependent) with TTL-based cleanup to avoid memory leaks
Admin dashboard shows current throttled JID count and throttle events in the last 24 hours
technicalNotes: Implement as middleware in `src/assistant/message-router.ts` before pipeline dispatch
Use a `Map<string, {count: number, windowStart: number}>` with periodic cleanup (every 5 minutes)
Default limits: 10 msg/60s; configurable `rateLimiting.perUserWindowMs` and `perUserMaxMessages` in settings.json
Distinct from `src/lib/frequency-cap.ts` (outbound cap) — this is inbound abuse prevention

userStories.title: Outbound media pre-send validation against WhatsApp size and format limits
userStories.description: When staff or automated workflows send media via `sendWhatsAppMedia`, there is no pre-send validation. Sending an oversized video (>16MB) or unsupported MIME type silently fails at the WhatsApp level with no actionable error surfaced to the admin.
acceptanceCriteria: Before sending, validate MIME type against WhatsApp-supported list: JPEG/PNG (images ≤5MB), MP4 (video ≤16MB, H.264+AAC only), AAC/MP3/OGG/AMR (audio ≤16MB), PDF/DOCX/XLSX (documents ≤100MB)
If validation fails, `sendWhatsAppMedia` throws a structured error with fields: `code: 'MEDIA_VALIDATION_FAILED'`, `reason`, `actualSizeMb`, `limitMb`
Admin API routes that call `sendWhatsAppMedia` return HTTP 422 with the validation error details
A unit test covers each unsupported type and the boundary size condition for images and videos
Validation is skipped when the media URL is a remote HTTPS URL (size cannot be pre-checked without fetching)
technicalNotes: `sendWhatsAppMedia` is in `src/lib/whatsapp/index.ts` — add a `validateMedia(buffer, mimeType)` helper called before `sock.sendMessage()`
WhatsApp size limits: image 5MB, video 16MB, audio 16MB, document 100MB, sticker 100KB
Add `src/lib/whatsapp/media-validator.ts` as a new file with exported `validateWhatsAppMedia()` function

userStories.title: CSP connect-src whitelist for AI provider endpoints used by admin dashboard
userStories.description: The current Helmet CSP sets `connect-src: ['self']`, which blocks the admin dashboard from making direct API calls to external services (e.g. health-checking AI provider endpoints, loading avatar URLs from WhatsApp CDN). Browser console errors accumulate silently and certain admin features fail without clear diagnostics.

A Vitest test verifies that the CSP header string contains the required connect-src values in production mode
No `unsafe-eval` or `unsafe-inline` directives are introduced
`img-src` is extended to include `https://pps.whatsapp.net data:` to allow WhatsApp avatar images in the dashboard
technicalNotes: Edit the `helmet()` call in `src/index.ts` — add to `connectSrc` array
AI provider base URLs can be derived from `src/assistant/data/settings.json` `providers[].baseUrl` at startup
Use `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` in development mode to catch violations without blocking

userStories.title: Human handoff SLA timer with breach alert to admin
userStories.description: When a conversation is escalated to human handoff, there is no mechanism to alert admin if no human responds within an SLA window. Customers left waiting after escalation have significantly higher churn rates than those who never reached a bot.
acceptanceCriteria: When an escalation event is created, a timer starts with configurable SLA duration (default: 15 minutes, configurable per profile as `handoff.slaDurationMinutes`)
If no outbound message is sent on the escalated conversation within the SLA window, an admin WhatsApp alert fires: 'SLA breach: [phone] has been waiting X minutes since escalation at [time]'
The alert includes the last user message for context
If a human replies before the SLA expires, the timer is cancelled and no alert is sent
SLA timer state is persisted to DB so it survives server restarts
Admin dashboard shows open handoffs with elapsed time and SLA status (green/amber/red)
technicalNotes: Integrate with `src/assistant/escalation.ts` — on escalation creation, insert a pending SLA record
Use a cron job (every 2 minutes) to check for breached SLAs rather than Node.js `setTimeout` (which doesn't survive restarts)
`escalation_events` table already exists — add `sla_breached_at` and `human_responded_at` columns via Drizzle migration
Detect human response by checking if an outbound message for that phone was sent after the escalation timestamp

userStories.title: System prompt A/B experiment framework for intent response quality
userStories.description: The AI system prompt is a single static configuration with no mechanism to test variants. Minor wording changes can produce 5-15% improvements in task completion rate, but there is currently no way to measure that. An experiment framework allows operators to define two prompt variants, split live traffic, and measure resolution rate and fallback rate per variant.
acceptanceCriteria: A new config section `experiments[].id, variants[].weight, variants[].systemPromptOverride` in settings.json is parsed and validated via Zod schema
Traffic is split by deterministic hash of the sender JID modulo total weight, ensuring the same user always gets the same variant within an experiment
Per-variant metrics (message count, fallback rate, CSAT score) are tracked in a new `experiment_metrics` DB table
Admin API `GET /api/rainbow/experiments/:id/results` returns variant comparison with confidence intervals
Experiments can be activated and deactivated without server restart via admin dashboard
When no experiment is active, system falls back to the default system prompt with zero overhead
technicalNotes: Add experiment resolution at the prompt-assembly step in the AI provider manager
Use `crypto.createHash('md5').update(phone + experimentId).digest('hex')` for deterministic assignment
Schema: `experiment_metrics(experiment_id, variant_id, phone_hash, message_count, fallback_count, csat_sum, window_date)`

userStories.title: Configurable data retention policy per-profile with admin UI controls
userStories.description: Data retention is currently hardcoded globally. Malaysia's PDPA Retention Principle requires retention periods to be set only as long as necessary for the stated purpose, and different profiles (hostel, cafe) have different legal and operational needs.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin UI settings tab shows current retention configuration per profile: `retention_days`, `grace_period_days`, `enabled` toggle
Operators can edit and save retention settings via the existing settings API without requiring a server restart
Preview pane shows count of records that would be soft-deleted and hard-deleted if purge ran now
Settings are validated: `retention_days` must be 30-3650, `grace_period_days` must be 7-365
When retention is disabled for a profile, an audit log entry is created recording who disabled it and when

userStories.title: PDPA data breach notification workflow with 72-hour commissioner deadline
userStories.description: Malaysia's amended PDPA (Phase 3, June 2025) mandates that data controllers notify the Personal Data Protection Commissioner within 72 hours of discovering a qualifying breach, and notify affected data subjects within 7 days. Rainbow AI stores WhatsApp message history and guest personal data, requiring a documented breach response workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: A new admin endpoint `POST /api/rainbow/security/breach-report` accepts a breach description and creates a timestamped breach record in a `pdpa_breach_log` table
On creation, the system automatically calculates and stores the 72-hour commissioner notification deadline and 7-day subject notification deadline
Admin WhatsApp notification is sent to the system admin with breach details and both deadlines
Admin dashboard shows open breach records with countdown timers to each deadline, colour-coded (green/amber/red)
Breach log is append-only; contains: reported_by, description, affected_count_estimate, commissioner_notified_at (nullable), subjects_notified_at (nullable)

Create `src/routes/admin/breach-report.ts` following the same pattern as `src/routes/admin/gdpr-erasure.ts`
Use existing `admin-notifier.ts` for the WhatsApp alert

userStories.title: WhatsApp media message acknowledgement in AI conversation flow
userStories.description: Guests frequently send images (booking confirmations, screenshots, receipts) and voice notes to the hostel WhatsApp. Rainbow AI currently only processes text messages and silently ignores media. Acknowledging media receipt with a context-aware response prevents users from thinking their message was lost.
acceptanceCriteria: Incoming image messages trigger a configurable static reply from the `media_received` static reply key

Incoming document messages trigger a `document_received` reply
Media messages are logged to `rainbow_messages` with `messageType: 'image'|'audio'|'document'` and `mediaUrl` (if available)

Media replies do not count against conversation fallback rate metrics
technicalNotes: Add media type detection in `src/assistant/pipeline/input-validator.ts` based on `IncomingMessage.messageType`

Route media messages to a dedicated `media-handler` stage that short-circuits the full NLP pipeline

userStories.title: Webchat widget consent banner with timestamped opt-in log
userStories.description: The webchat widget collects and processes personal data (chat content) without presenting a data processing consent notice. GDPR and Malaysia's PDPA both require explicit informed consent before initiating data collection. Industry audits find 47% of chatbots lack this, representing a compliance vulnerability.
acceptanceCriteria: On first widget load, a consent banner is shown before the chat interface with [Accept] and [Decline] options
If the user declines, the chat interface is not rendered and a privacy policy link is shown
If the user accepts, the acceptance is stored in `localStorage` with timestamp and not shown again for 365 days
The consent timestamp and a truncated session ID are sent to `POST /api/webchat/consent-log` and persisted to DB
The consent banner is keyboard-accessible and meets WCAG 2.1 AA
Consent text content is configurable per profile via admin settings
technicalNotes: Add consent check at the top of `src/public/js/modules/chat-send.js` before any message is sent
Consent log table: `webchat_consent_log(session_id_hash, accepted_at, profile_id, user_agent_hash)`
Use `localStorage.setItem('rb_consent', JSON.stringify({accepted: true, ts: Date.now()}))` for persistence

userStories.title: Baileys DB auth state health check and corruption recovery at startup
userStories.description: Baileys session credentials stored in PostgreSQL can become corrupted during a crash mid-transaction. The next reconnection attempt will silently fail with a malformed session error, requiring manual DB intervention. An automatic health check at startup should detect and clear corrupted auth state before attempting connection.
acceptanceCriteria: At server startup, before calling `makeWASocket`, a `validateAuthState(instanceId)` check queries DB auth rows and verifies JSON parseability of credential fields
If validation fails (unparseable JSON, missing required creds fields), corrupted rows are deleted and the QR pairing flow is re-initiated
An admin WhatsApp notification is sent: '[instanceId] auth state was corrupted and cleared — please re-scan QR code'
Validation results are logged at INFO level: `[DbAuth:pelangi] Auth state healthy: creds OK, 42 signal keys`
A new admin endpoint `GET /api/rainbow/instances/:id/auth-health` returns auth state validity without triggering recovery
technicalNotes: Add `validateAuthState(instanceId: string)` to `src/lib/whatsapp/db-auth-state.ts`
Check: `SELECT key, value FROM wa_auth_state WHERE instance_id = $1` — attempt `JSON.parse(value)` for each row
Required credential fields for a valid Baileys session: `noiseKey`, `signedIdentityKey`, `registrationId`, `advSecretKey`
Call validation from `WhatsAppInstance.start()` before `useDbAuthState()` in `src/lib/whatsapp/instance.ts`

userStories.title: Structured data notice sent to user on first WhatsApp interaction
userStories.description: When a guest initiates their first WhatsApp conversation with the bot, they receive no notification that their messages will be stored and processed. PDPA's Notice and Choice Principle requires data subjects to be informed of collection purposes at or before collection.
acceptanceCriteria: On the very first message from a new JID (no prior `rainbow_conversations` record), a data notice follows the normal welcome response
Notice text is configurable in `knowledge.json` under key `data_notice_first_contact`

userStories.title: Webhook HMAC signature validation for incoming Meta Cloud API events
userStories.description: Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API signs incoming webhook payloads with HMAC-SHA256 using the app secret. acceptanceCriteria: All requests to `POST /webhooks/meta` are rejected with HTTP 403 if the `X-Hub-Signature-256` header is absent or invalid

When validation fails, the rejection is logged at WARN level with the source IP
If `META_APP_SECRET` environment variable is not set, validation is skipped with a startup WARNING log
A unit test covers: valid signature passes, tampered body fails, missing header fails
technicalNotes: `req.rawBody` is already captured in `src/index.ts` via `captureRawBody` middleware
Add `validateMetaSignature(req)` middleware to `src/routes/webhooks/index.ts`
Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()` for constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks
Header format: `X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex-digest>`

userStories.title: POS webhook receiver: push confirmed orders to kitchen display system

userStories.title: WABA webhook subscription health check on server startup

technicalNotes: Use the existing Meta Graph API token stored in env vars

userStories.title: WhatsApp media auto-download: save incoming images/documents before URL expiry

userStories.title: Tiered confidence-based fallback with progressive escalation

acceptanceCriteria: A per-JID failure counter is maintained in conversation state, reset on successful intent classification
On first failure: bot asks user to rephrase in a friendly tone
On second consecutive failure: bot presents a quick-reply list of 4-5 core capabilities
On third consecutive failure: bot sends a human handoff message and notifies staff
Failure counter resets after any successful intent classification
All fallback events are logged in intent_analytics with failure_tier (1, 2, or 3)

Quick-reply options are profile-specific (hostel vs. cafe) and configurable in settings.json

userStories.title: Order modification window after submission: allow item changes before kitchen acceptance

acceptanceCriteria: After order confirmation, the bot informs the customer they have N minutes to make changes (configurable via settings.json)

Once the window expires (or kitchen accepts via POS webhook), modification requests are rejected with a polite explanation

If no POS integration is active, the modification window still applies against a timer-based lock

Cart re-opening reuses the existing conversational cart add/remove flow

userStories.title: Proactive abandoned-cart recovery message on WhatsApp session idle
userStories.description: When a customer has items in their cart and the WhatsApp conversation goes idle for a configurable period (default: 30 minutes) without confirming the order, send a proactive WhatsApp message reminding them of their cart and offering to resume or clear it. acceptanceCriteria: When a WhatsApp conversation has an active non-empty cart and no activity for the configured idle period, a single recovery message is sent

If user replies 'Resume order', the conversation resumes from the cart confirmation step
If user replies 'Clear cart' or the recovery message is ignored for 24 hours, the cart is cleared
Recovery idle period is configurable per-profile in settings.json
technicalNotes: Implement a cart_idle_timer per-JID, stored in conversation state with setTimeout or a cron-based checker
Use the existing outbound WhatsApp send mechanism for the proactive message
Comply with WhatsApp 24-hour session window: recovery message must be sent within 24h of the last user message

Track recovery_message_sent boolean in cart state to prevent duplicate messages

Focus is not stolen from the input field when new messages arrive

Avoid aria-live='assertive' which interrupts current screen reader output

userStories.title: Pre-arrival automated WhatsApp message sequence for confirmed hostel bookings

userStories.title: Persist raw webhook payloads to durable storage before processing

The DLQ entry references the raw event ID so operators can replay the original payload
GET /admin/dlq/:jobId returns the associated raw event payload
Vitest test asserts raw event is persisted even when downstream processing throws

Retention policy: raw events should be pruned by the existing data-retention scheduler after 30 days

userStories.title: Webchat widget dark mode support via CSS prefers-color-scheme

userStories.title: Admin dashboard multi-user RBAC: viewer vs operator vs super-admin roles

Middleware: checkRole(['operator', 'super-admin']) applied to mutating routes

userStories.title: LLM response faithfulness check: flag answers that contradict the knowledge base
userStories.description: Rainbow AI performs Zod schema validation and structured retries on LLM responses but has no semantic check that the answer is grounded in KB content. acceptanceCriteria: After generating a KB-backed answer, a secondary check verifies key facts in the answer appear in the retrieved KB chunks
If faithfulness score < 0.7 and a KB chunk exists, the answer is replaced with a conservative 'please check with our team' fallback
faithfulness_score is logged in intent_analytics for monitoring

Vitest test: inject a KB chunk with 'check-in: 2pm' and assert a response containing 'check-in: 3pm' is flagged

Expensive approach: second LLM call with 'Does the answer contradict the context? YES/NO'
Reference: https://www.getmaxim.ai/articles/llm-hallucination-detection-and-mitigation-best-techniques/
Start with lightweight approach; gate the expensive approach behind a feature flag

userStories.title: Chatbot conversation containment rate KPI on admin analytics dashboard

userStories.title: LLM provider cost budget alert: notify when daily spend exceeds configurable threshold

userStories.title: Update WhatsApp cost tracker for per-message pricing model (July 2025)

technicalNotes: Locate existing cost tracking in `src/routes/admin/whatsapp-cost.ts` and `src/assistant/__tests__/whatsapp-cost.test.ts`

userStories.title: Webchat widget offline hours banner with configurable business hours
userStories.description: The webchat widget is always-open with no indication of business operating hours. An unavailability banner set by configurable business hours improves user expectations.
acceptanceCriteria: Business hours are configurable per-profile in admin settings: `businessHours.timezone`, `businessHours.schedule` (array of day/open/close)

The input field remains functional (messages can still be sent and will be answered by AI or queued for human review)
Business hours configuration is exposed via `GET /api/webchat/config/:profile` for client-side rendering
Public holiday override can be configured as a list of dates in settings
technicalNotes: Business hours logic should be evaluated server-side in `src/routes/public/webchat-api.ts` and included in the initial widget config payload

userStories.title: Admin audit log for configuration changes with before/after diff
userStories.description: Any admin can modify AI system prompts, routing rules, and intent configurations with no record of who changed what and when. When the bot starts behaving unexpectedly after a config change, operators cannot determine root cause. PDPA's Data Integrity Principle also requires that processing decisions be accountable.
acceptanceCriteria: Every write operation through the config API (`PUT /api/rainbow/config/*`, settings updates) inserts a record into `rainbow_config_audit` with: admin_user, endpoint, before (JSON), after (JSON), timestamp
Admin dashboard shows an audit log tab with the last 100 config change events, filterable by date range and admin user
Each audit entry shows a human-readable diff (changed keys highlighted)
Audit records are retained for 365 days (not subject to standard conversation retention policy)
Verify `rainbow_config_audit` table is being populated by ALL config write paths, not just current partial coverage
technicalNotes: `rainbow_config_audit` table already exists — audit routes in `src/routes/admin/config.ts` to identify which write paths are missing
Add an `auditConfigChange(adminUser, endpoint, before, after)` helper and call it from all config mutation routes
The before-value must be captured BEFORE the write — common bug to avoid

userStories.title: Repeat order shortcut: AI waiter offers to repeat last order for returning guests
userStories.description: If a returning guest has a previous order on record, the AI waiter should proactively offer to repeat it at the start of the conversation. This reduces friction for regulars and makes the experience feel personalised.
acceptanceCriteria: On session start, check FnB MCP for last order by guest JID or phone
If found within last 30 days, AI offers to repeat previous order
Guest reply YES loads previous order into cart as starting point
Guest reply NO proceeds to normal browsing flow
If no prior order found, normal welcome message shown
technicalNotes: Call FnB MCP get_order_history with jid and limit 1 on webchat session init
Trigger only for webchat widget not WhatsApp to avoid unsolicited messages
Last order check is best-effort and fails silently if MCP unavailable

userStories.title: Upsell suggestions: AI waiter recommends add-ons after main item is ordered
userStories.description: After a guest adds a main item to the cart, the AI waiter should make one natural upsell suggestion such as a drink pairing or add-on based on the item category. Should feel conversational and never pushy and suggested once per session max.

Suggestion fetched from FnB MCP get_upsell_suggestions or category-based fallback

Guest can accept to add to cart, decline, or ignore with no follow-up if declined
Upsell only triggered once per session regardless of how many items are added

If MCP has no upsell endpoint, use category-based hardcoded map: rice to drink, cake to coffee
Keep suggestion message to one sentence max

userStories.title: Post-order feedback: AI waiter requests a quick star rating after order is served
userStories.description: After an order is marked as served by the kitchen, the AI waiter should send a follow-up message asking for a simple 1 to 5 star rating. This captures real-time guest satisfaction and surfaces issues before guests leave a bad review elsewhere.

Rating stored via FnB MCP submit_feedback or in rainbow_messages table

Feedback only requested once per order

Check feedbackRequested: boolean in session state before sending
Store rating and orderId in rainbow_messages or new order_feedback table
Low rating alert optionally notifiable to admin via existing admin-notifier.ts

userStories.title: Popular items suggestion: AI waiter proactively recommends top-ordered dishes when guest is undecided

userStories.title: WhatsApp message reaction emoji as lightweight CSAT signal
userStories.description: Process incoming WhatsApp reaction events (emoji reactions to bot messages) and use them as lightweight feedback signals — mapping thumbs-up/thumbs-down reactions to positive/negative CSAT signals without requiring the user to complete a full star-rating flow. acceptanceCriteria: Incoming webhook events of type 'reaction' are parsed and not silently discarded
Thumbs-up reaction on a bot message increments the positive CSAT counter for that conversation session
Thumbs-down reaction triggers a follow-up message asking the user what went wrong (optional short text reply)
Reaction data is stored in conversation_feedback table with message_id, emoji, and timestamp
Reaction handling is profile-agnostic (works for both Pelangi and Makan Moments)
technicalNotes: Baileys emits reaction events in the messages.upsert event as a message with a reaction key
WhatsApp Cloud API reaction webhook: messages[].type == 'reaction', with reaction.message_id and reaction.emoji fields
Map emoji to sentiment: thumbs-up/heart = positive, thumbs-down = negative, others = neutral/ignored

userStories.title: WhatsApp Business Calling API: click-to-call escalation button

userStories.title: Webchat widget progressive disclosure onboarding for first-time visitors

userStories.title: WhatsApp template category auto-validator: warn on rejection risk before submission
